title: Dynamic Launch Signal Orchestrator — booking windows, signal pulses, and capacity lanes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As product teams scale simultaneous launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces we lack a single operational model for booking launch windows, communicating launch 'signals' (canary pulses, traffic ramps), and reserving capacity lanes. Current practice is ad-hoc Slack/RFC threads and manual spreadsheets which causes contention, late discovery of capacity conflicts, and manual back-and-forth with infra and SREs.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight Launch Signal Orchestrator: a coordinated calendar + simple API + runbook that lets teams request booking windows (with metadata: region, peak qps, expected SLO risk), reserve capacity lanes for Dedicated/Hosted, and surface 'signal pulses' for staged canaries. The system must integrate with Console dashboards and provide a daily digest for on-call and launch owners.

Scope & Deliverables:
- Booking API v0 (HTTP) for teams to request and reserve launch windows with structured metadata.
- Cadence matrix artifact: standard pulse templates (smoke, small cohort, full ramp) and timing defaults per surface (runtime/console/api).
- Capacity lane semantics: definitions for 'reserve', 'hedge', and 'burst' lanes + overflow fallback policy.
- Cross-train calendar UI view in Console (prototype) with capacity heatmap and conflict alerts.
- Runbook and cutover checklist, plus a rehearsal checklist for cross-team dry-runs.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Strict enforcement vs advisory booking: opt for advisory first (soft gates + alerts) to preserve developer velocity; move to enforced reservations for P0 launches after iteration.
- Centralized single-pane-of-glass vs federated desks per org: implement a single canonical calendar with per-team ownership metadata (scales better for reporting).
- Automated capacity hedging vs manual SRE sign-off: start with suggested hedges generated from historical telemetry and require SRE ack for high-risk windows.

Phases:
1) Discovery & templates (2 wks): interviews, cadence matrix, pulse templates.
2) Booking API + proto calendar (3 wks): minimal API + Console prototype and heatmap.
3) Integrations & runbook (2 wks): integrate with Dedicated capacity signals, add digest emails and on-call alerts.
4) Rehearsal & launch (1 wk): run two cross-team rehearsals and onboard 2 pilot teams.

Success metrics:
- Pilot adoption: 2 product teams using booking API for real launches within 6 weeks.
- Reduction in cross-team capacity conflicts reported in Launch Retro by 50%.
- Time-to-book (request -> acknowledged) under 24 hours for advisory bookings.
acceptance_criteria: Cadence matrix published in Confluence with 3 pulse templates and per-surface defaults
Booking API v0 deployed to staging with documentation and an example client
Console prototype shows calendar view + capacity heatmap and can flag conflicts
Runbook and rehearsal checklist reviewed and signed off by SRE and Platform PMs
Two pilot teams complete dry-run and provide feedback that is triaged
